provider: Software Heritage Archive (CAPI read side) + Save Code Now (anonymous crawl trigger)

free_tier.stated: No storage quota is imposed on the depositor, because the depositor never uploads bytes. The archive stores content-addressed git objects from public repositories, deduplicated by sha1_git, and growth is the Foundation's problem, not yours. Live scale reference: the `torvalds/linux` origin is at visit 500 ('visit':500, date 2026-10-18). Deposit (push) is separate and capped: swh-deposit docs say 'upload limitation of 100Mib', and the source default in swh/deposit/config.py is "max_upload_size": 209715200 (200 MiB).

retention.stated: list-rate-limited, and this is the binding constraint on reading a large tree (walking a repo = 1 call per directory). retention: permanent and intrinsic - this is a preservation archive, deletion is not part of the model; `visit_status: full` snapshots are retained per visit

egress.terms: Free and unmetered - no pricing page, no billing, a public research archive. Downloads are direct `GET .../raw/` byte streams from Varnish. Note there is no CDN requirement to satisfy: nothing to pay.

tooling: Official Web API v1 (documented route index at https://archive.softwareheritage.org/api/1/); Python `swh.model`/`swh.web.client`; no rclone backend. Read paths: /api/1/origin/<url>/get/, /api/1/origin/<url>/visit/latest/, /api/1/snapshot/<id>/, /api/1/revision/<id>/, /api/1/directory/<id>/, /api/1/content/sha1_git:<h>/raw/.
chaining: This is the strongest chaining object in the niche and it is NOT a place to upload - it is a place to make arbitrary public git content addressable and permanent. The mechanism: POST /api/1/origin/save/git/url/<URL>/ anonymously, with no account and no key, and it returns {"save_task_status":"pending","loading_task_id":422136312}. So: unlimited free git hosts (one repo each, any size) -> anonymous SWH crawl request per URL -> content permanently in SWH under a sha1_git you can fetch forever. The upload-to-SWH step costs zero bytes of your quota; the bytes live in the free git host and SWH becomes the durability + retrieval layer. Multiply by unlimited origins. Combine with round-1's GitHub Releases finding: the archive is a free permanence layer over storage you already have.
limits_note: per-object-cap (deposit only): 100 MiB documented, 200 MiB default in swh-deposit config. request-rate: SWH CAPI sends `X-Ratelimit-Limit: 120` / `X-Ratelimit-Remaining` / `X-Ratelimit-Reset` (observed 114->118 remaining across calls) - 120 requests per window per IP, i.e. list-rate-limited, and this is the binding constraint on reading a large tree (walking a repo = 1 call per directory). retention: permanent and intrinsic - this is a preservation archive, deletion is not part of the model; `visit_status: full` snapshots are retained per visit. Write access: /api/1/origin/save/ is open anonymously; deposit.softwareheritage.org returns 401 to anonymous PUT/POST.
reliability_note: Read path is reliable but rate-shaped: 120 req/window/IP will throttle a naive tree walk of a 20 TiB corpus - parallelise across IPs or batch directory listings. docs.softwareheritage.org sits behind Anubis PoW (proof-of-work bot wall) and returns a challenge page with upstream_status 200, so doc numbers must be taken from the GitHub source, not the docs site. Anonymous save requests are queued ('pending'), not instant - ingestion lag is hours to days.
